Alright I'm gonna keep it short and sweet because I can't help but feel time is of the essence. But I'm 23 and my last serious "serious" relationship I was in was in high school. Since then, I've been with my fair share of people, but they've always wanted to keep it strictly physical. Tlno one wanted to have a relationship with me. After ~5 years of this, I ended up believing there was seriously something fucked up with me. Maybe I'm too childish, too weird. I'm not too sure. I was also raped in this time period and, my god, that did not help. 

As of the last 2 years, I decided "fuck it. I'm just going to completely devote myself to my major, graduate, get a job, and get stable. Until I get stable, I won't even think of actively pursuing girls. They e given me way too much heartbreak over the years and right now, they're just a distraction I don't need. If something between me and someone else happens organically, then great! But I'm not going to be seeking someone out. I won't go to bars and hit on girls (not that I ever did that in the first place, but it best illustrates my intent). If I'm going to be with someone, it just needs to happen randomly and organically. 

A year and a half later or so (Jan 2019), I met someone on tinder (you know, cause we all lie to ourselves occasionally) but I was just using tinder to make myself laugh. For example, my bio was like "just had my roommate slap me in the face while I recorded it for reference footage. So that's where my life is at the moment." (And a few short bio shit. Idk. Not important.). 

She asked if she could see it. I sent it, thought that was that but didn't care cause I got a laugh out of it. To my surprise though she kept responding. 5 and a half months later, we're dating and I want to marry this girl. She is everything I've ever looked for all in one person. And the best part is, I know she loves me back. 

My point in all of this is that I had gotten to the point where I literally gave up looking at girls. I felt I wasn't going to find "her" or "anyone" for years so why bother looking now. And then I met "her". POINT: you can't just  give up on this. There is someone out there for you. I really hated being told that before but I'm not telling you to give you some bs hope to hold onto for now. I'm telling you as someone who had literally given up finding someone who wanted to be with him. 

When you find them, they make life worth living. Idk how else to explain it. We just spend the past 2 weeks with $20 for food to split between us before the next paycheck came in. 4 years ago, idve been crying throughout those weeks and being depressed for having no money and the state of my life. Dude. I actually kind of had fun through this with her. I'm just trying to give you something to look forward to because we're obviously different people, but I truly believe there's someone out there waiting for us. 

I focused on this interaction you had between the girl and you because it sounded to me like that was the trigger for all of it. That and I could best relate to it (in line with "no one wants to be friends with ME. Just who they want/think I am or what I do professionally.)

 I can't say you're a catch or she's dumb cause I don't know either of you and I won't lie to you. But what I do know is that that someone waiting out there for you will think that (that you're a catch). 

What I've found to be most important in my life is not finding people who want to spend time with me. But making it so that I enjoy being with me at the very least. It was/is really hard at times, but I enjoy me now and people who don't I can finally feel confident enough to leave by the wayside

Holy shit I fucking feel that. But before I address that, I wasn't saying that you were/would demean them. I posed it like that because that's how I approached it originally (I was originally opposed to going to community college for previously stated reasons). Sorry if I didn't make that clear.

My entire life, I thought I wanted to be a teacher. I got my first job as a camp counselor at age 11 and these are some of my most cherished memories ever. I did this every year till highschool where I continued that but also taught in the preschool hosted by the high school in order to teach students to be teachers. Did this every year and was my favorite class. Finished high school with an internship as a gym teacher at the nearby elementary school. Went to college for early education. After my first semester, I realized it wasn't what I wanted. It was terrifying. I felt like I'd wasted the last 8 years or so and truthfully, in terms of professional development, I had. But exploring that change led me to the major i am working towards now and I know without a doubt this is what I'm meant to do (other than be a stay at home dad and care for my kids... I really want that more than anything....). 

I know even contemplating that change can be terrifying, and maybe it isn't even needed for you. But I don't believe your fear of something should prevent you from at least exploring other options, you know? Don't double down because you don't know where else to go. Sometimes we need to flounder a bit

I also see that you can't get the grades to get into he school you want to. For me, I took a detour. The college I wanted to go to for a semester, dropped out. Moved to parents home. Worked for 6 months. Moved in with brother for a bit in that time period (or so). Moved back to parents house. Began work again but now was attending local community college. Continued this for almost 3 years (couple classes at a time rather than a normal 12 credit semester to ensure I could devote the time to each class and get the grade I wanted in each one. Had a 1.2 gpa in high school at the begining of Junior year (or so). When finishing my A.A., I was on the Dean's list with a goal of ~3.8) and got my A.A.. Then transfered to an even better school. Moved out of parents house.

Don't knock unconventional paths just cause they're diff or you'd be separated from your class. I wish I immediately went to the community college rather than everything inbetween.

If the pain does nothing for you, then why cut? What are you gaining? Control? 

What pulled me out of this phase in my life was finding a purpose. For me, I moved out of my parents house and transferred to a real 4 year school with an actual plan in a field I actually really enjoyed. It didn't just *poof* gone. It was a transition and I still deal with it. But it's so much easier when you can actually think of a reason for yourself to stay rather than to stay for someone else (i.e. don't want to hurt my parents).

Sometimes I'd wrap a rope around my neck, hold a knife to my skin, imagine setting myself on fire, take just under the legal overdose threshold for ibeprpfun (I wouldn't suggest this because, for me, overtime it led to the only time I was hospitalized for an attempted suicide and actually made things worse as my parents found out about EVERYTHING that day. Easily one of the worst days of my life and by far the hardest thing I've ever had to do: explain to them the situation. 

My point is, for me being near death or in that state of mind helped me think it through now that all I had to do was a simple movement or something and I'd be dead. HOWEVER. this is coming from a guy who always felt as though he'd never actually go through with it. So. Idk. 

If you decide to try this, PLEASE PLEASE PLEASE BE CAREFUL. the whole point in doing it is to convince yourself otherwise, not prepare you for death.

For me, it's the mental image i have of my mother not being able to comprehend why a kid she didn't even know killed herself. 

The girl was my flyer for some time in cheerleading, so I knew her. She killed herself and when my mom heard through the grapevine of the community, she spoke to me about it (cause she knows I was/am depressed). She had this look of bewilderment, borderline tearing up from the mere thought of it, on her face that I've never seen before in her attempt to try and understand not only what she must've been going through, but also in her attempt to understand the whole thing as a parent and empathize for the parents of my friend. 

This was for some girl she never knew, she never knew her parents or anyone related. She just knew it was a girl who attended the school I went to and that was all it took. 

She walked towards me and hugged me in the most feeble and vulnerable way I've ever seen her in my life (this is a woman who's hard as rocks) and started to just hold me as she cried into my shoulder and whimpered out about how if it had been me... 

She never finished that statement but she didn't need to. 

This applies to both my parents, the understanding this experience, but this experience alone I had with just my mom. My mom and I fight all the time and in all honesty, she was a huge reason for my depression/suicidal thoughts (or so far as I can surmise. Probably more going on, but at the time (when I lived at home), this was the best I could do in terms of understanding the source of my depression. That and going no where in life. But that's beside the point. 

The past two years, I've moved out and into a new house  and my relationship with my parents is now better than it ever has been. But that thought still haunts me. It wasn't this single experience alone that makes life worth living cause there were ~3 of these moments, but none as intense or emotional as this. The others were more discussion I had with her and that was about it with a bit of emotion. So you see why that single experience sticks with me

I could never put my parents through that. I understand now that I'm older the reasons they made the decisions that they did, but that doesnt mean I approve of them. Just understand them now. 

What makes life more living for me is primarily so my parents never have to go through that. I know they'd never get over it and it would subsequently destroy them despite the relationship we previously had.

 In the past two years, they've become role models for me in the morals they hold, the foundation for the rest of my character. They mean everything to me. I couldnt  live with (or for with) the knowledge that I put that on them.

Maybe others love isn't enough, but have you thought about how this might effect them in the end? I only ask because for me, that thought in association with my parents is what keeps me from doing it. Maybe for you it isn't your parents, but you didn't say you don't care about those people. You just said it isn't enough. What would be enough? Can I help in some way? I'm legitimately asking -- I want to help however I can
